subject: Advice on how to get MCMC to better explore sample space?

messages.author: 08d7d872077e52b9
messages.subject: Advice on how to get MCMC to better explore sample space?
parts:
Hi All,

I've been trying to use MCMC on an SIR-style model, and I've managed to get everything running without errors, but my sampling is very inefficient (see traceplots below). I'm currently using the default "RW sampler", I tried two parameters to "AF_slice" just to see what would happen, and it made the process considerably slower. I'm assuming I need to use more appropriate samplers? But I have no idea how to start thinking about that! 

Here is a reproducible version of the code I am using (runs with attached function and C file):

library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(deSolve)
library(nimble)
library(readxl)
library(tidyr)
setwd("C:/Users/dms228/R Scripts/nimble")
source("model1_v9_functions.R")

#######################################################################################
##                                        SET UP                                     ##
#######################################################################################
N        = 4850000
Io0      = N * 0.0003
Ih0      = N * 0.0007
B0       = 30000000
R0       = 3500000
S0       = N - Io0 - Ih0 - R0
z.init   = c(S = S0, Io = Io0, Ih = Ih0, R = R0, B = B0, NI = 0)

sim.start.date <- as.Date("1989-12-31")
data.start.date <-  as.Date("1998-12-31")
end.date <- as.Date("2019-12-31")
dates <- seq(from = sim.start.date, to = end.date, by = "1 day")
month.date.mapper <- data.frame(date = dates) %>%
  mutate(month = month(date)) %>%
  mutate(year = year(date)) %>%
  mutate(month.abs = month + 12*(year - 1990)) %>%
  mutate(index = 0:(length(dates)-1)) %>%
  filter(date >= data.start.date)
month.final.day <- month.date.mapper[!duplicated(month.date.mapper$month.abs,fromLast = TRUE),]
final.day.index <- month.final.day[,"index"]

num.days <- 11200
M <- length(dates) - 1
ts <- seq(0,M)
t <- seq(0,M+11)

temp <- 20 + 5*sin(t/58)
pre <- 10 + 8*sin(t/58 - 60)

#######################################################################################
##                                    DATA SIMULATION                                ##
#######################################################################################
#system("R CMD SHLIB v6b_sim.c") #Create .dll file
dyn.load("v6b_sim.dll")
Lambda <- 10
omega <-0.1
p <- 0.0045
epsilon <- 10
t <- seq(1,length(temp))
temp.mat <- cbind(time = t, temp = temp)
pre.mat <- cbind(time = t, temp = pre)

ode.sim.C<- solveDE_C(z.init, parms = c(Lambda, omega, p, epsilon))[-1,2:7]
data <- traj_2_data(ode.sim.C)

n.months <- length(data)

#######################################################################################
##                                     NIMBLE MODEL                                  ##
#######################################################################################

Model <- nimbleCode({
  for (i in 1:n.months) {
    y[i] ~ dpois(z[i])
  }
  z[1:n.months] <- nimODE(z.init = z.init[1:6], Lambda = Lambda, omega = omega, p = p, epsilon = epsilon)
  ## Priors
  Lambda ~ dunif(min = 0, max = 20)  # dgamma(3,0.6)        # Lambda
  omega ~ dunif(min = 0, max = 3)  # dgamma(10,1)         # omega
  p ~ dbeta(1,3)        # p
  epsilon ~ dunif(min = 0, max = 30)                          # epsilon
})
Consts <- list(n.months = n.months)
nimbleData <- list(y = data, z.init = z.init)
inits <- list(Lambda = 1, omega = 1, p = 0.1, epsilon = 0.1)
RNimbleModel <-
  nimbleModel(
    code = Model,
    name = 'nimbleModel',
    constants = Consts,
    data = nimbleData,
    inits = inits
  )
CNimbleModel <- compileNimble(RNimbleModel, showCompilerOutput = TRUE)
RModelMCMC <- buildMCMC(RNimbleModel)
CModelMCMC <-compileNimble(RModelMCMC, project = RNimbleModel, showCompilerOutput = TRUE)

CModelMCMC$run(1000, time = TRUE)
CModelMCMC$getTimes()

samplesNew <- as.matrix(CModelMCMC$mvSamples)
par(mfrow = c(1, 4))
plot(samplesNew[ , "Lambda"], type = "l", xlab = "iteration",
     ylab = "Lambda")
plot(samplesNew[ , "omega"], type = "l", xlab = "iteration",
     ylab = "omega")
plot(samplesNew[ , "p"], type = "l", xlab = "iteration",
     ylab = "p")
plot(samplesNew[ , "epsilon"], type = "l", xlab = "iteration",
     ylab = "epsilon")

Thank you!

Best,
Debbie

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Advice on how to get MCMC to better explore sample space?
parts:
Hi Debbie,

A couple suggestions:

1) You might simply try univariate slice samplers on each scalar parameter.
2) You might try Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) using our beta release of HMC (see r-nimble.org/ad-beta), which should be released fully soon.

-Chris

messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Re: Advice on how to get MCMC to better explore sample space?
parts:
Hi Debbie

I've not looked at the details of your model, but see right away from your figures that you are sampling rates that are very close to zero - the lower bound on the paramter space.  In which case you could try using the nimbleNoBounds package to sample on the log transformed scale
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/nimbleNoBounds/vignettes/nimbleNoBounds.html

 All the best
David
